docs.title: Traefik
docs.text: Traefik is the reverse proxy and load balancer for all Nomad-managed services. It automatically discovers services via the Nomad provider and uses a wildcard TLS certificate issued from Vault PKI.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Property Value Nomad Job traefik Image traefik:v3.6 Type system (runs on all Nomad nodes) Ports 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), 8081 (Dashboard) Network Mode Host Storage GlusterFS host volume mounted at /data TLS Wildcard cert (*.<dns-suffix>) from Vault PKI Cert location /srv/gluster/nomad-data/traefik/tls/cert.pem and key.pem

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Traefik is deployed by Layer 2 Terraform (terraform/services/nomad-jobs.tf). It is always the first service deployed and is a prerequisite for all other services that need HTTPS access through the reverse proxy.

To redeploy Traefik (and re-issue the wildcard TLS certificate):

./setup.sh --dev
# Select: d9) Deploy Traefik only

Or use Layer 2 Terraform directly:

docker compose run terraform-services apply -auto-approve -target=nomad_job.traefik

docs.title: TLS Configuration
docs.text:
Traefik does not use ACME or cert-manager. Instead, a wildcard certificate is issued directly from the Vault intermediate CA (pki_int/) at deploy time:

  • Certificate: *.<dns-suffix>
  • SANs: *.<dns-suffix>, <dns-suffix>
  • TTL: 1 year
  • Issuer: Vault pki_int/ intermediate CA
  • Storage: /srv/gluster/nomad-data/traefik/tls/ (on GlusterFS)

No certResolver tags

Nomad service tags use tls=true only. There is no certresolver tag. Traefik serves the wildcard certificate as the default TLS certificate for all HTTPS connections via a file provider configuration at /data/traefik/config/tls.yml.

Vault 1.21.x ACME nonce bug

Vault 1.21.x has a bug in its ACME endpoint that causes nonce errors. Wildcard cert issuance via Vault's PKI secrets engine (/v1/pki_int/issue/) works correctly and is used instead.

To re-issue the certificate (e.g., after expiry or DNS suffix change), redeploy Traefik via option d9. The Layer 2 null_resource.install_traefik_cert always issues a fresh certificate on apply.

docs.title: Service Discovery
docs.text:
Traefik discovers services via the Nomad provider:

--providers.nomad=true
--providers.nomad.endpoint.address=http://127.0.0.1:4646
--providers.nomad.exposedByDefault=false
--providers.nomad.namespaces=default

Services opt into Traefik routing by setting traefik.enable=true in their Nomad service tags. Services without this tag are not exposed through Traefik.

docs.title: Routing Rules
docs.text:
Each service defines its routing via Nomad service tags. Services accept both FQDN and short hostname:

"traefik.http.routers.vault.rule=Host(`vault.<dns-suffix>`) || Host(`vault`)"

Entrypoints:

Entrypoint Port Purpose web 80 HTTP (no redirect to HTTPS by default) websecure 443 HTTPS with wildcard TLS traefik 8081 Dashboard (insecure, admin access only)

docs.title: Authentik Forward Auth
docs.text:
Traefik is configured to use Authentik as a forward auth provider for protecting admin services. This is configured via a static middleware file at /data/traefik/config/authentik.yml (on GlusterFS), rendered from nomad/config/traefik/authentik.yml.

Services that require authentication add the middleware tag:

"traefik.http.routers.pihole.middlewares=authentik@file"

Services accessible to all authenticated users (like Kasm) use a different outpost URL.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Traefik dashboard is available at: 

http://<nomad01-ip>:8081

Or via DNS (through Traefik itself): 

https://traefik.<dns-suffix>

The dashboard shows all configured routers, services, middlewares, and entrypoints.

docs.title: HA Configuration
docs.text:
When ha_traefik_enabled: true is set in bootstrap.yml, Traefik runs as a system job on all Nomad nodes and keepalived VRRP manages a VIP that floats to the highest-priority healthy node.

See High Availability Configuration for setup instructions.

docs.title: 404 errors for a service
docs.text:
Check that the service is registered in Nomad and has the correct tags:

# List registered services
nomad service list

# Check Traefik's view of routers
curl http://<nomad01-ip>:8081/api/http/routers | jq .

# Check services
curl http://<nomad01-ip>:8081/api/http/services | jq .

docs.title: TLS certificate missing or expired
docs.text:
Redeploy Traefik to re-issue the wildcard certificate:

./setup.sh --dev
# d9) Deploy Traefik only

Verify the certificate:

echo | openssl s_client -connect vault.<dns-suffix>:443 2>/dev/null | \
  openssl x509 -noout -dates

docs.title: Service not discovered by Traefik
docs.text:
1. Verify traefik.enable=true is in the service tags
  2. Check the service is running: nomad job status <service>
  3. Check Traefik logs: nomad alloc logs -job traefik
  4. Verify the Nomad service is registered: nomad service list

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy Traefik using the setup menu:

./setup.sh
# Select option 7: Deploy Traefik

Or deploy directly with the Nomad CLI:

docker compose run --rm nomad job run /nomad/jobs/traefik.nomad.hcl

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before deploying Traefik, the following must be in place:

  1. Nomad cluster -- All three Nomad nodes operational
  2. Pi-hole DNS -- DNS records for services must resolve to nomad01
  3. Step-CA -- Certificate Authority running and reachable at ca.<dns_postfix>
  4. GlusterFS -- Shared volume mounted at /srv/gluster/nomad-data on all Nomad nodes

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    CLIENT[Client] -->|:80| HTTP[Entrypoint<br/>web]
    CLIENT -->|:443| HTTPS[Entrypoint<br/>websecure]

    HTTP --> ROUTER_HTTP[HTTP Routers]
    HTTPS --> ROUTER_HTTPS[HTTPS Routers]

    ROUTER_HTTP --> SERVICES[Nomad Services]
    ROUTER_HTTPS --> SERVICES

    HTTPS -->|ACME| STEPCA[step-ca]

    subgraph nomad["Nomad Service Discovery"]
        VAULT_SVC[vault :8200]
        AUTH_SVC[authentik :9000]
    end

    SERVICES --> nomad

Traefik runs in host networking mode on nomad01, binding directly to ports 80, 443, and 8081. All service DNS records (e.g., vault.<domain>, auth.<domain>) point to nomad01's IP address, so Traefik receives all inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic and routes it to the appropriate backend.

docs.title: Entrypoints
docs.text:
Traefik defines three entrypoints:

Entrypoint Port Purpose web 80 HTTP traffic and ACME HTTP-01 challenges websecure 443 HTTPS traffic with TLS termination traefik 8081 Dashboard and API (insecure mode)

docs.title: Service Discovery
docs.text:
Traefik uses the Nomad provider to automatically discover services registered in the Nomad cluster:

--providers.nomad=true
--providers.nomad.endpoint.address=http://127.0.0.1:4646
--providers.nomad.exposedByDefault=false
--providers.nomad.namespaces=default
--providers.nomad.allowEmptyServices=true

Key behaviors:

  • exposedByDefault=false -- Services must explicitly opt in with traefik.enable=true in their Nomad service tags.
  • allowEmptyServices=true -- Prevents Traefik from removing routes when a service temporarily has zero healthy instances.
  • Traefik connects to the local Nomad agent at http://127.0.0.1:4646 since it runs on nomad01 in host networking mode.

docs.title: Enabling a Service for Traefik
docs.text:
Nomad services opt in to Traefik routing by setting tags on their service stanza. For example, Vault registers itself as:

service {
  name     = "vault"
  port     = "api"
  provider = "nomad"

  tags = [
    "traefik.enable=true",
    "traefik.http.routers.vault-http.rule=Host(`vault.mylab.lan`) || Host(`vault`)",
    "traefik.http.routers.vault-http.entrypoints=web",
    "traefik.http.routers.vault.rule=Host(`vault.mylab.lan`) || Host(`vault`)",
    "traefik.http.routers.vault.entrypoints=websecure",
    "traefik.http.routers.vault.tls=true",
    "traefik.http.routers.vault.tls.certresolver=step-ca",
    "traefik.http.services.vault.loadbalancer.server.port=8200",
  ]
}

Each service defines two routers:

  • An HTTP router (entrypoint web) for plain HTTP access and ACME challenges.
  • An HTTPS router (entrypoint websecure) with TLS enabled via the step-ca certificate resolver.

docs.title: Router Rules
docs.text:
All routers accept both the FQDN and the short hostname:

Host(`service.<dns_postfix>`) || Host(`service`)

This means https://vault.mylab.lan and https://vault both reach the same backend.

docs.title: ACME Certificate Management
docs.text:
Traefik automatically obtains TLS certificates from the internal step-ca using ACME:

--certificatesresolvers.step-ca.acme.email=admin@<dns_postfix>
--certificatesresolvers.step-ca.acme.storage=/data/traefik/acme.json
--certificatesresolvers.step-ca.acme.caserver=https://ca.<dns_postfix>/acme/acme/directory
--certificatesresolvers.step-ca.acme.httpchallenge=true
--certificatesresolvers.step-ca.acme.httpchallenge.entrypoint=web

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Traefik
    participant StepCA as step-ca

    Client->>Traefik: HTTPS request for vault.mylab.lan
    Note over Traefik: No cert cached for this domain

    Traefik->>StepCA: ACME new-order (vault.mylab.lan)
    StepCA-->>Traefik: HTTP-01 challenge token

    Note over Traefik: Serves token on :80/.well-known/acme-challenge/

    StepCA->>Traefik: GET /.well-known/acme-challenge/[token]
    Traefik-->>StepCA: Challenge response

    StepCA->>StepCA: Validate challenge
    StepCA-->>Traefik: Signed certificate

    Traefik->>Traefik: Store cert in /data/traefik/acme.json
    Traefik-->>Client: TLS response with valid certificate

docs.title: CA Trust
docs.text:
Since step-ca uses a private root CA, Traefik must trust it to complete ACME requests. Two environment variables configure this:

Variable Value Purpose SSL_CERT_FILE /data/certs/root_ca.crt System-level CA trust for Go's TLS LEGO_CA_CERTIFICATES /data/certs/root_ca.crt LEGO ACME library CA trust

The root CA certificate is stored on the GlusterFS volume at /srv/gluster/nomad-data/certs/root_ca.crt, which is mounted into the container at /data/certs/root_ca.crt.

docs.title: Certificate Storage
docs.text: ACME certificates are persisted at /data/traefik/acme.json on the GlusterFS volume. This file is preserved across container restarts so certificates do not need to be re-issued.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
Traefik registers itself as a Nomad service with an HTTP health check:

service {
  name     = "traefik"
  port     = "dashboard"
  provider = "nomad"

  check {
    type     = "http"
    path     = "/ping"
    port     = "dashboard"
    interval = "10s"
    timeout  = "2s"
  }
}

The /ping endpoint is enabled via --ping=true and bound to the traefik entrypoint on port 8081.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Traefik dashboard provides a web interface to inspect routers, services, and middleware. It is enabled in insecure mode (no authentication) for lab use:

--api=true
--api.dashboard=true
--api.insecure=true

Access the dashboard at:

http://nomad01:8081/dashboard/

Trailing Slash Required

The dashboard URL must include the trailing slash: /dashboard/. Without it, Traefik returns a 404.

docs.title: Useful API Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose http://nomad01:8081/api/http/routers List all HTTP routers http://nomad01:8081/api/http/services List all HTTP services http://nomad01:8081/api/entrypoints List entrypoints http://nomad01:8081/ping Health check

Query routers to verify service discovery:

curl -s http://nomad01:8081/api/http/routers | jq .

docs.title: Verifying the Deployment
docs.text:
After deploying Traefik, verify it is running correctly:

# Check job status
docker compose run --rm nomad job status traefik

# Check allocation logs
docker compose run --rm nomad alloc logs -job traefik

# Verify the service is registered
docker compose run --rm nomad service list

# Test the ping endpoint
curl http://nomad01:8081/ping

# Check discovered routers
curl -s http://nomad01:8081/api/http/routers | jq '.[].rule'

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
404 Not Found for a service

Traefik is running but cannot route the request to a backend.

  1. Check that the service is registered in Nomad: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad service list
  2. Verify the router exists in Traefik: 
    curl -s http://nomad01:8081/api/http/routers | jq .
  3. Confirm DNS resolves the service hostname to nomad01's IP: 
    nslookup vault.mylab.lan
  4. Check that the service's Nomad tags include traefik.enable=true.
ACME certificate challenges failing

Traefik cannot obtain a TLS certificate from step-ca.

  1. Verify step-ca is running and reachable: 
    curl -k https://ca.mylab.lan/health
  2. Check that DNS resolves the service domain to nomad01 (step-ca must be able to reach Traefik on port 80 for HTTP-01 challenges).
  3. Inspect the ACME storage file for errors: 
    ssh nomad01 'cat /srv/gluster/nomad-data/traefik/acme.json | jq .'
  4. Clear stale ACME data and restart the job: 
    ssh nomad01 'rm /srv/gluster/nomad-data/traefik/acme.json'
docker compose run --rm nomad job stop -purge traefik
docker compose run --rm nomad job run /nomad/jobs/traefik.nomad.hcl
Service not discovered by Traefik

The service is running in Nomad but does not appear in Traefik's router list.

  1. Verify the service is healthy in Nomad: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad job status <job-name>
  2. Check that the service uses provider = "nomad" (not Consul).
  3. Confirm the service tags include traefik.enable=true.
  4. Inspect Traefik logs for discovery errors: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad alloc logs -job traefik
Port 80 or 443 already in use

Another process is binding to Traefik's ports on nomad01.

  1. Identify what is using the port: 
    ssh nomad01 'sudo ss -tlnp | grep -E ":80|:443"'
  2. Stop/purge any stale Traefik allocations: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad job stop -purge traefik

docs.title: Uptime Kuma
docs.text: Uptime Kuma is a self-hosted service health monitoring tool with a clean web UI. It monitors service endpoints and provides status pages, alerting, and uptime statistics.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Property Value Nomad Job uptime-kuma Image louislam/uptime-kuma:2 Node Pinned to nomad01 Port 3001 Storage /srv/gluster/nomad-data/uptime-kuma/ (GlusterFS) Embedded DB MariaDB (v2 — not compatible with v1 SQLite data)

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Select option 5 from the setup menu:

./setup.sh
# 5) Uptime Kuma (monitoring)

docs.title: First-Time Setup
docs.text:
Uptime Kuma does not support environment variable-based admin provisioning. After deployment:

  1. Browse to https://status.<dns-suffix>
  2. Create the first admin account
  3. Configure monitors for your services

Authentik protection

The status page is protected by Authentik forward auth when accessed through Traefik. After you create an admin account, you can optionally disable the built-in auth: Settings > Security > Disable Auth.

docs.title: Suggested Monitors
docs.text:
Configure these monitors to track your lab's health:

Name Type URL Notes Vault HTTP http://<nomad01-ip>:8200/v1/sys/health?uninitcode=200&sealedcode=200 Sealed/uninitialized counts as healthy Authentik HTTP http://<nomad01-ip>:9000/-/health/live/ Live health endpoint Traefik HTTP http://<nomad01-ip>:8081/ping Ping endpoint Nomad HTTP http://<nomad01-ip>:4646/v1/status/leader Leader election Pi-hole HTTP http://<dns-01-ip>/admin/ Admin page Vault PKI HTTP https://vault.<dns-suffix>/v1/sys/health Use -k for self-signed

docs.title: DNS
docs.text:
The status page is accessible via: 

https://status.<dns-suffix>

The DNS record status.<dns-suffix> is created automatically by Layer 2 Terraform when Uptime Kuma is deployed.

docs.title: Not accessible via Traefik
docs.text:
# Check Traefik knows about the router
curl http://<nomad01-ip>:8081/api/http/routers | jq . | grep uptime

# Check Nomad service is registered
ssh labadmin@nomad01 "nomad service list | grep uptime"

docs.title: Container not starting
docs.text: ssh labadmin@nomad01 "nomad alloc logs -job uptime-kuma"

docs.title: Lost admin access
docs.text:
Reset by clearing data (loses all monitor configuration):

ssh labadmin@nomad01 "sudo rm -rf /srv/gluster/nomad-data/uptime-kuma/*"
# Then stop and restart the job
ssh labadmin@nomad01 "nomad job stop uptime-kuma"
# Redeploy via setup.sh option 5

docs.title: Vault
docs.text: HashiCorp Vault provides secrets management and internal PKI for the lab. It is deployed by Layer 1 Terraform and configured by Layer 2.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Property Value Nomad Job vault Image hashicorp/vault:1.21.4 Type service (count 1) Node Pinned to nomad01 Ports 8200 (API/UI), 8201 (Cluster) Network Mode Host Storage Docker bind mount /srv/gluster/nomad-data/vault:/data/vault Privileged Yes (required for GlusterFS writes) Resources 200 MHz CPU, 256 MB memory TLS Enabled after Phase 2 bootstrap (self-signed via its own PKI)

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy Vault using the setup menu:

./setup.sh
# Select option 8: Deploy Vault

Or deploy directly with the Nomad CLI:

docker compose run --rm nomad job run /nomad/jobs/vault.nomad.hcl

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before deploying Vault, the following must be in place:

  1. Nomad cluster -- All three Nomad nodes operational
  2. Traefik -- Reverse proxy running for HTTPS access at vault.<dns_postfix>
  3. Pi-hole DNS -- vault.<dns_postfix> resolving to nomad01
  4. GlusterFS -- Shared volume mounted at /srv/gluster/nomad-data on all Nomad nodes

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph clients["Clients"]
        BROWSER[Browser / CLI]
    end

    subgraph nomad01["nomad01"]
        TRAEFIK[Traefik<br/>:80 / :443]
        VAULT[Vault<br/>:8200]
        NOMAD[Nomad Agent<br/>:4646]
    end

    subgraph storage["GlusterFS"]
        VDATA["/srv/gluster/nomad-data/vault"]
    end

    BROWSER -->|HTTPS| TRAEFIK
    TRAEFIK -->|HTTP :8200| VAULT
    VAULT --> VDATA
    NOMAD -->|JWT (WIF)| VAULT

    subgraph jobs["Nomad Jobs"]
        AUTH_JOB[Authentik]
        SAMBA_JOB[Samba AD]
    end

    NOMAD -->|Sign JWT| jobs
    jobs -->|Present JWT| VAULT
    VAULT -->|Return secrets| jobs

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Privileged mode -- The Docker container runs as privileged (privileged = true) because GlusterFS FUSE mounts require elevated permissions for file writes.
  • Direct bind mount -- Vault uses a Docker bind mount (/srv/gluster/nomad-data/vault:/data/vault) instead of a Nomad host volume. This ensures Vault has direct access to the GlusterFS path.
  • TLS disabled -- Vault listens on plain HTTP (tls_disable = true) because Traefik handles TLS termination. Vault is only accessible within the host or through Traefik.
  • disable_mlock -- Set to true because the Nomad Docker driver does not allow the IPC_LOCK capability. In a home lab environment this is an acceptable trade-off.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Vault's configuration is rendered as a Nomad template at /local/vault.hcl inside the container:

ui = true
disable_mlock = true

storage "file" {
  path = "/data/vault"
}

listener "tcp" {
  address     = "0.0.0.0:8200"
  tls_disable = true
}

api_addr     = "http://<nomad01_ip>:8200"
cluster_addr = "http://<nomad01_ip>:8201"
Setting Value Purpose ui true Enables the Vault web UI disable_mlock true Required for Nomad Docker driver storage.file.path /data/vault Persistent storage on GlusterFS listener.tls_disable true Traefik terminates TLS api_addr http://<ip>:8200 Advertised API address cluster_addr http://<ip>:8201 Cluster communication address

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text: On first deployment, Vault starts in an uninitialized state. The setup script automatically initializes it with a single key share and single threshold -- appropriate for a home lab where operational simplicity is preferred over the security of Shamir's Secret Sharing with multiple key holders.

docs.title: Initialization Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Rationale Key shares 1 Single unseal key for simplicity Key threshold 1 One key required to unseal

docs.title: Initialization Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Setup as setup.sh
    participant Vault
    participant FS as crypto/vault-credentials.json

    Setup->>Vault: GET /v1/sys/health
    Vault-->>Setup: 501 (not initialized)

    Setup->>Vault: PUT /v1/sys/init (shares=1, threshold=1)
    Vault-->>Setup: unseal_key + root_token

    Setup->>Vault: PUT /v1/sys/unseal (key)
    Vault-->>Setup: 200 (unsealed)

    Setup->>FS: Save credentials
    Note over FS: unseal_key, root_token,<br/>vault_address, initialized_at

    Setup->>Vault: Enable KV v2 secrets engine
    Setup->>Vault: Configure JWT auth for Nomad WIF
    Setup->>Vault: Create per-job roles and policies

docs.title: Credential Storage
docs.text:
After initialization, credentials are saved to crypto/vault-credentials.json (gitignored):

{
  "unseal_key": "<base64-encoded-key>",
  "root_token": "hvs.xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "vault_address": "http://192.168.1.50:8200",
  "initialized_at": "2026-02-22T12:00:00Z"
}

Security Warning

This file contains the root token and unseal key. Protect it accordingly:

  • It is gitignored and must never be committed
  • Back it up to a secure location
  • Losing the unseal key means Vault data cannot be recovered after a restart

docs.title: Unseal Process
docs.text:
Vault seals itself on every restart. Before it can serve requests, it must be unsealed with the key from crypto/vault-credentials.json.

The setup script handles unsealing automatically during deployment. For manual unsealing:

# Using the Vault CLI
export VAULT_ADDR="http://nomad01:8200"
vault operator unseal <unseal_key>

# Or using the HTTP API
curl -X PUT http://nomad01:8200/v1/sys/unseal \
  -d '{"key": "<unseal_key>"}'

Auto-Unseal

For production environments, Vault supports auto-unseal using cloud KMS or Transit secrets engines. This lab uses manual unseal for simplicity.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
Vault's health check is configured to accept all operational states as healthy, since an uninitialized or sealed Vault is expected during first deployment:

check {
  type     = "http"
  path     = "/v1/sys/health?standbyok=true&uninitcode=200&sealedcode=200"
  port     = "api"
  interval = "10s"
  timeout  = "3s"
}
Parameter Effect standbyok=true Standby nodes report healthy uninitcode=200 Uninitialized Vault returns 200 instead of 501 sealedcode=200 Sealed Vault returns 200 instead of 503

docs.title: Traefik Integration
docs.text:
Vault registers with Nomad using Traefik-compatible service tags:

tags = [
  "traefik.enable=true",
  "traefik.http.routers.vault-http.rule=Host(`vault.<domain>`) || Host(`vault`)",
  "traefik.http.routers.vault-http.entrypoints=web",
  "traefik.http.routers.vault.rule=Host(`vault.<domain>`) || Host(`vault`)",
  "traefik.http.routers.vault.entrypoints=websecure",
  "traefik.http.routers.vault.tls=true",
  "traefik.http.routers.vault.tls.certresolver=step-ca",
  "traefik.http.services.vault.loadbalancer.server.port=8200",
]

This creates two routers:

  • vault-http -- HTTP access on port 80 (also handles ACME challenges)
  • vault -- HTTPS access on port 443 with a TLS certificate from step-ca

Access Vault at:

  • https://vault.<dns_postfix> (HTTPS via Traefik)
  • http://nomad01:8200 (direct, no TLS)

docs.title: KV v2 Secrets Engine
docs.text:
Vault uses the KV version 2 secrets engine at the path secret/. KV v2 provides versioned secrets with metadata, soft-delete, and rollback capabilities.

The setup script enables KV v2 automatically during initialization:

vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2

docs.title: Storing Secrets
docs.text:
# Store Authentik secrets
vault kv put secret/authentik \
  secret_key="<random-string>" \
  postgres_password="<random-string>"

# Store Samba AD secrets
vault kv put secret/samba-ad \
  admin_password="<domain-admin-password>"

docs.title: Reading Secrets
docs.text:
vault kv get secret/authentik
vault kv get -field=secret_key secret/authentik

docs.title: Workload Identity Federation (WIF)
docs.text: WIF allows Nomad jobs to authenticate to Vault using short-lived JWT tokens instead of long-lived Vault tokens. This eliminates the need to store any Vault credentials on Nomad nodes.

docs.title: How WIF Works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Job as Nomad Job
    participant Nomad as Nomad Server
    participant Vault

    Note over Nomad: Job has vault { role = "authentik" }

    Nomad->>Nomad: Sign JWT with job identity claims
    Nomad->>Job: Inject JWT via NOMAD_TOKEN

    Job->>Vault: Authenticate at auth/jwt-nomad/login<br/>with JWT + role "authentik"
    Vault->>Nomad: Fetch JWKS from /.well-known/jwks.json
    Nomad-->>Vault: Public keys

    Vault->>Vault: Validate JWT signature + claims
    Vault-->>Job: Short-lived Vault token<br/>(scoped to "authentik" policy)

    Job->>Vault: GET secret/data/authentik
    Vault-->>Job: Secrets (secret_key, postgres_password)

docs.title: JWT Auth Configuration
docs.text:
Vault is configured with a JWT auth backend at path jwt-nomad:

Setting Value Purpose Auth path jwt-nomad JWT auth mount point JWKS URL http://<nomad01_ip>:4646/.well-known/jwks.json Nomad's public key endpoint Audience vault.io Expected JWT audience claim

docs.title: Nomad Default Identity
docs.text:
Nomad servers are configured with a default_identity block that tells Nomad how to sign JWTs for jobs that request Vault access:

vault {
  enabled = true
  default_identity {
    aud = ["vault.io"]
    ttl = "1h"
  }
}

docs.title: Per-Job Roles
docs.text:
Each service that needs Vault access has a dedicated role that maps JWT claims to a Vault policy:

Role Job Policy Secret Path authentik authentik authentik secret/data/authentik samba-dc samba-dc samba-dc secret/data/samba-ad

In the Nomad job file, services declare their Vault role:

vault {
  role        = "authentik"
  change_mode = "restart"  # Restart task if secrets change
}

docs.title: Vault Policies
docs.text: Policies define what each role can access. All policies are stored in nomad/vault-policies/.

docs.title: authentik.hcl
docs.text:
Allows the Authentik job to read its secrets:

# Allow reading Authentik secrets
path "secret/data/authentik" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow listing and reading metadata (for debugging)
path "secret/metadata/authentik" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}

docs.title: samba-dc.hcl
docs.text:
Allows the Samba AD job to read its secrets:

# Allow reading Samba AD secrets (admin password, sync credentials)
path "secret/data/samba-ad" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow listing and reading metadata (for debugging)
path "secret/metadata/samba-ad" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}

docs.title: nomad-server.hcl
docs.text:
Allows Nomad servers to create and manage tokens for jobs:

# Allow creating tokens against the "nomad-cluster" role
path "auth/token/create/nomad-cluster" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

# Allow looking up the "nomad-cluster" role
path "auth/token/roles/nomad-cluster" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow looking up own token capabilities
path "auth/token/lookup-self" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow looking up incoming tokens for validation
path "auth/token/lookup" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

# Allow revoking tokens via accessor when jobs end
path "auth/token/revoke-accessor" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

# Allow renewing own token
path "auth/token/renew-self" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

docs.title: Verifying the Deployment
docs.text:
After deploying Vault, verify it is running correctly:

# Check job status
docker compose run --rm nomad job status vault

# Check Vault health (returns initialized/sealed status)
curl -s http://nomad01:8200/v1/sys/health | jq .

# Check seal status
curl -s http://nomad01:8200/v1/sys/seal-status | jq .

# Verify Vault is registered as a Nomad service
docker compose run --rm nomad service list

# Check allocation logs
docker compose run --rm nomad alloc logs -job vault

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Permission denied on storage

Vault cannot write to its storage path on GlusterFS.

  1. Verify the container is running in privileged mode: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad job inspect vault | jq '.Job.TaskGroups[].Tasks[].Config.privileged'
  2. Clean up stale data and redeploy: 
    ssh nomad01 'sudo rm -rf /srv/gluster/nomad-data/vault/*'
docker compose run --rm nomad job stop -purge vault
docker compose run --rm nomad job run /nomad/jobs/vault.nomad.hcl
Port 8200 already in use

A previous Vault allocation may still be running.

  1. Check for stale allocations: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad job status vault
  2. Stop and purge the job, then redeploy: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad job stop -purge vault
docker compose run --rm nomad job run /nomad/jobs/vault.nomad.hcl
Vault not responding

Vault may be sealed, uninitialized, or scheduled on an unexpected node.

  1. Check which node Vault is running on: 
    docker compose run --rm nomad job status vault
  2. Check seal status: 
    curl -s http://nomad01:8200/v1/sys/seal-status | jq .
  3. If sealed, unseal it: 
    curl -X PUT http://nomad01:8200/v1/sys/unseal \
  -d '{"key": "<unseal_key_from_credentials_file>"}'
  4. If uninitialized, run the setup menu option 8 to initialize.
WIF authentication failing for a job

A Nomad job cannot authenticate to Vault using its JWT.

  1. Verify the JWT auth backend is enabled: 
    export VAULT_ADDR="http://nomad01:8200"
vault auth list
  2. Check the role exists: 
    vault read auth/jwt-nomad/role/<role-name>
  3. Verify Nomad's JWKS endpoint is reachable from Vault: 
    curl -s http://nomad01:4646/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .
  4. Check the Nomad job's vault stanza specifies the correct role name.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• :octicons-arrow-right-24: Authentik -- Identity provider that retrieves secrets from Vault
  • :octicons-arrow-right-24: Samba AD -- Active Directory that retrieves secrets from Vault
  • :octicons-arrow-right-24: Traefik -- Reverse proxy that routes traffic to Vault

docs.title: Adding Active Directory Users
docs.text: Users can be added to the Samba AD domain via two methods: LDAP Account Manager (LAM) web UI or the samba-tool CLI.

docs.title: Method 1: LDAP Account Manager (LAM)
docs.text: LAM provides a web interface for managing AD users and groups.

docs.title: Accessing LAM
docs.text:
Via DNS: 

https://lam.<dns-suffix>

Protected by Authentik forward auth (admin group required).

docs.title: LAM Login
docs.text:
LAM uses a bind account (lam-admin) to connect to AD. The LAM master password is generated by Terraform and stored in Vault.

Get the LAM bind password: 

vault kv get -field=lam_bind_password secret/samba-ad/service-accounts

On the LAM login page: - Select profile: lam - Enter the lam-admin password

docs.title: Creating a User
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Users tab
  2. Click Create user
  3. Fill in:
  4. First name, Last name
  5. Username (sAMAccountName)
  6. Password (must meet domain complexity policy)
  7. Email (optional)
  8. Click Save

docs.title: Creating a Group
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Groups tab
  2. Click Create group
  3. Enter group name
  4. Add members
  5. Click Save

docs.title: Method 2: samba-tool CLI
docs.text: Connect to the Samba AD container and use samba-tool directly.

docs.title: Accessing the Samba Container
docs.text:
# SSH to nomad01, find the container
ssh labadmin@nomad01

# Find the DC01 container
CONTAINER=$(docker ps --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | grep 'samba-ad' | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')

# Open a shell
docker exec -it $CONTAINER /bin/bash

docs.title: Creating a User
docs.text:
# Basic user
samba-tool user create john.doe 'SecurePassword123!'

# With full details
samba-tool user create jane.doe 'SecurePassword123!' \
  --given-name="Jane" \
  --surname="Doe" \
  --mail-address="jane.doe@mylab.lan" \
  --telephone-number="555-1234"

# Set password to never expire
samba-tool user setexpiry jane.doe --noexpiry

docs.title: Creating a Group and Adding Members
docs.text:
# Create group
samba-tool group add "IT Admins"

# Add user to group
samba-tool group addmembers "IT Admins" jane.doe

# Verify membership
samba-tool group listmembers "IT Admins"

docs.title: Resetting a Password
docs.text: samba-tool user setpassword john.doe --newpassword='NewSecurePassword456!'

docs.title: Disabling/Enabling Users
docs.text:
# Disable
samba-tool user disable john.doe

# Enable
samba-tool user enable john.doe

docs.title: Listing Users
docs.text:
# List all users
samba-tool user list

# Show details for a user
samba-tool user show john.doe

docs.title: Organizational Units (OUs)
docs.text:
The following OUs are created automatically during Samba AD deployment:

OU Purpose CN=Users Default user container (service accounts) OU=Workstations Computer accounts for domain-joined workstations OU=Service Accounts Dedicated service accounts

To create a custom OU for lab users:

# Via samba-tool
samba-tool ou create "OU=Lab Users,DC=mylab,DC=lan"

# Move a user to the OU
samba-tool user move john.doe "OU=Lab Users,DC=mylab,DC=lan"

docs.title: Service Accounts
docs.text:
The following service accounts are created automatically:

Account Purpose Credentials location domain-join-svc Domain join operations for NAS/workstations secret/samba-ad/service-accounts authentik-sync Read-only LDAP bind for Authentik user sync secret/samba-ad/service-accounts lam-admin LDAP Account Manager bind account secret/samba-ad/service-accounts

Do not delete these accounts. They are managed by Terraform.

docs.title: Authentik Sync
docs.text:
If Authentik AD sync is configured (authentik_ad_sync: true in bootstrap.yml), users created in Samba AD are automatically synced to Authentik within the configured interval (default: 5 minutes).

To trigger an immediate sync:

  1. Log in to Authentik admin (https://auth.<dns-suffix>)
  2. Navigate to Directory > Federation and Social login
  3. Find Samba AD source
  4. Click Run sync

Or via the Authentik API: 

API="https://auth.<dns-suffix>/api/v3"
TOKEN=$(vault kv get -field=api_token secret/authentik)

# Get source slug
curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/sources/ldap/" | jq '.results[].slug'

# Trigger sync
curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -X POST "$API/sources/ldap/samba-ad/sync/"

docs.title: Domain Password Policy
docs.text:
The default Samba AD password policy requires: - Minimum 7 characters - Complexity enabled (uppercase, lowercase, digit or symbol) - No account lockout by default

To view or change the policy:

# View policy
samba-tool domain passwordsettings show

# Change minimum length
samba-tool domain passwordsettings set --min-pwd-length=12

# Enable account lockout after 5 failed attempts
samba-tool domain passwordsettings set \
  --account-lockout-threshold=5 \
  --account-lockout-duration=30 \
  --reset-account-lockout-after=5

docs.title: High Availability Configuration
docs.text: This tutorial covers enabling keepalived VRRP high availability for DNS and Traefik. HA provides a Virtual IP (VIP) that floats between nodes, so a single node failure does not interrupt service.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• 3-node Proxmox cluster (HA with a single node provides no benefit)
  • Core lab stack deployed (option 1 completed)
  • Available IP addresses in your network for VIPs (outside DHCP range)

docs.title: Planning Your VIPs
docs.text:
Choose two IPs that are: - In your lab network CIDR - Outside your router's DHCP range - Not in use by any other device

Choose two VRRP router IDs that are: - Between 1 and 255 - Unique — not used by other VRRP/HSRP devices on your network (routers often use low numbers)

Example plan: - DNS VIP: 192.168.1.3/24, VRRP ID 51 - Traefik VIP: 192.168.1.100/24, VRRP ID 53

docs.title: Configure bootstrap.yml
docs.text:
Add the HA settings to bootstrap.yml:

ha_dns_enabled: true
ha_dns_vip: "192.168.1.3/24"         # Choose an unused IP
ha_dns_vrrp_router_id: 51             # Choose an unused VRRP ID (1-255)
ha_dns_vrrp_password: "pihole1"       # Max 8 characters

ha_traefik_enabled: true
ha_traefik_vip: "192.168.1.100/24"   # Choose an unused IP
ha_traefik_vrrp_router_id: 53
ha_traefik_vrrp_password: "trafk1"   # Max 8 characters

docs.title: Apply HA Configuration
docs.text:
From the setup menu, select option 2:

./setup.sh
# 2) Enable HA (keepalived VIPs)

This reads the HA settings from bootstrap.yml and: 1. Updates terraform/terraform.tfvars with the HA variables 2. Applies Layer 1 Terraform (configures keepalived on VMs and LXCs) 3. Updates terraform/services/terraform.tfvars with the VIP addresses 4. Applies Layer 2 Terraform (updates DNS records to point to VIPs)

Bootstrap.yml change detection

The setup menu detects changes in bootstrap.yml on startup. If HA settings are detected but not yet applied, the menu prompts you to apply them with option *.

docs.title: Reconfiguring Client DNS
docs.text:
After enabling DNS HA, update your DNS server setting to use the VIP instead of a specific Pi-hole node IP. This ensures DNS continues to work even if one node fails.

Router DHCP settings (recommended): Change the DNS server to the DNS VIP.

macOS: 

networksetup -setdnsservers Wi-Fi 192.168.1.3

Linux: 

echo "nameserver 192.168.1.3" | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf

docs.title: DNS HA
docs.text:
# Verify VIP is bound on the master node
ssh labadmin@dns-01 "ip addr show eth0 | grep 192.168.1.3"

# Check keepalived status
ssh labadmin@dns-01 "systemctl status keepalived"

# Test DNS resolution through the VIP
dig @192.168.1.3 google.com

# Test failover: stop Pi-hole on master
ssh labadmin@dns-01 "sudo systemctl stop pihole-FTL"

# VIP should move to dns-02 within a few seconds
ssh labadmin@dns-02 "ip addr show eth0 | grep 192.168.1.3"

# DNS still resolves
dig @192.168.1.3 google.com

# Restore Pi-hole on dns-01
ssh labadmin@dns-01 "sudo systemctl start pihole-FTL"
# VIP moves back to dns-01 (preemptive mode)

docs.title: Traefik HA
docs.text:
# Verify VIP is bound on nomad01
ssh labadmin@nomad01 "ip addr show eth0 | grep 192.168.1.100"

# Check keepalived status on all Nomad nodes
for node in nomad01 nomad02 nomad03; do
  echo "=== $node ==="
  ssh labadmin@$node "systemctl status keepalived | grep -E 'Active|State'"
done

# Test Traefik through the VIP
curl -sk https://192.168.1.100/ -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"

# Test failover: stop Nomad job on master
ssh labadmin@nomad01 "nomad job stop traefik"

# VIP moves to nomad02
ssh labadmin@nomad02 "ip addr show eth0 | grep 192.168.1.100"

# Traefik still responds
curl -sk https://192.168.1.100/ -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"

# Restart Traefik
./setup.sh --dev  # d9) Deploy Traefik only

docs.title: VIP not bound on any node
docs.text:
Check keepalived is running and the VRRP auth is correct:

# Check logs on all nodes
ssh labadmin@dns-01 "journalctl -u keepalived -n 50"
ssh labadmin@dns-02 "journalctl -u keepalived -n 50"

Common causes: - VRRP password mismatch between nodes (must match exactly, max 8 chars) - VRRP router ID conflict with another device on the network - firewall blocking VRRP multicast (protocol 112)

docs.title: VIP on wrong node
docs.text:
Check priorities. nomad01 should be priority 101, nomad02 = 100, nomad03 = 99:

ssh labadmin@nomad01 "cat /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf | grep priority"

If priorities are wrong, re-apply Layer 1 Terraform.

docs.title: Split-brain (VIP on multiple nodes)
docs.text:
Check network connectivity between nodes. Keepalived uses VRRP multicast (224.0.0.18). If nodes cannot communicate, each thinks it is the master.

# Test multicast reachability
ssh labadmin@nomad01 "ping -c 3 nomad02"

docs.title: VRRP authentication failing
docs.text:
The VRRP password is limited to 8 characters. If your password is longer, keepalived silently truncates it, which may cause mismatches between nodes.

Verify all nodes use exactly the same password (check keepalived.conf on each node).

docs.title: Importing the Root CA Certificate
docs.text:
All internal services use TLS certificates issued by Vault PKI. Your browser and operating system do not trust this CA by default, so you will see certificate warnings when accessing services like https://vault.<dns-suffix> or https://auth.<dns-suffix>.

Importing the root CA certificate into your system's trust store eliminates these warnings.

docs.title: Download the Root CA
docs.text:
The root CA certificate is available from the Vault PKI endpoint:

curl -sk https://<nomad01-ip>:8200/v1/pki/ca/pem -o proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt

Or copy it from GlusterFS on any Nomad node:

scp labadmin@<nomad01-ip>:/srv/gluster/nomad-data/certs/root_ca.crt proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt

docs.title: System-wide (all browsers except Firefox/Zen)
docs.text:
1. Double-click proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt — Keychain Access opens
  2. Select the System keychain (or login for current user only)
  3. Click Add
  4. Find the certificate in Keychain Access (search for "Proxmox Lab")
  5. Double-click the certificate, expand Trust
  6. Set When using this certificate to Always Trust
  7. Close the window, enter your password to confirm

Or via command line:

sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
  -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt

docs.title: Firefox / Zen Browser
docs.text:
Firefox and Zen use their own certificate store — the system keychain is not used.

Zen Browser

Zen blocks untrusted CAs entirely with no bypass option. You must import the root CA for Zen to access any internal HTTPS services.

  1. Open Settings (or about:preferences)
  2. Search for Certificates
  3. Click View Certificates
  4. Go to the Authorities tab
  5. Click Import, select proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt
  6. Check Trust this CA to identify websites
  7. Click OK

docs.title: System-wide
docs.text:
1. Double-click proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt
  2. Click Install Certificate
  3. Select Local Machine (requires admin), click Next
  4. Select Place all certificates in the following store
  5. Click Browse, select Trusted Root Certification Authorities
  6. Click Next, then Finish

Or via PowerShell (admin):

Import-Certificate -FilePath proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt `
  -CertStoreLocation Cert:\LocalMachine\Root

docs.title: Firefox on Windows
docs.text: Same as the Firefox steps above — Firefox uses its own store on all platforms.

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu
docs.text:
sudo cp proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
sudo update-ca-certificates

docs.title: RHEL / Fedora / CentOS
docs.text:
sudo cp proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/
sudo update-ca-trust

docs.title: Arch Linux
docs.text:
sudo cp proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt /etc/ca-certificates/trust-source/anchors/
sudo trust extract-compat

docs.title: iOS / iPadOS
docs.text:
1. Transfer proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt to the device (AirDrop, email, or web)
  2. Open the file — a Profile Downloaded notification appears
  3. Go to Settings > General > VPN & Device Management
  4. Tap the profile, then Install
  5. Go to Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust Settings
  6. Enable full trust for the root certificate

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
1. Transfer proxmox-lab-root-ca.crt to the device
  2. Go to Settings > Security > Encryption & credentials
  3. Tap Install a certificate > CA certificate
  4. Select the file and confirm

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After importing, verify that your browser trusts the internal CA:

# Should show the full certificate chain without errors
curl -v https://vault.<dns-suffix>/v1/sys/health 2>&1 | grep "SSL certificate verify ok"

# Or test in browser — no certificate warning should appear
open https://vault.<dns-suffix>

docs.title: Certificate Renewal
docs.text:
The root CA has a 10-year TTL. The intermediate CA has a 5-year TTL. Wildcard service certificates have a 1-year TTL and are re-issued by re-running setup.sh option 1 or the Traefik deploy (d9).

If the root CA is regenerated (full purge + redeploy), you will need to re-import the new certificate on all client devices.

docs.title: Kasm LDAP Authentication with Samba AD
docs.text: This tutorial connects Kasm Workspaces to Samba AD so users can log in with their domain credentials. The credentials pass through to VM sessions (SSH, RDP, VNC) so users don't have to re-enter them.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Samba AD deployed (option 4)
  • Kasm deployed (option 3)
  • At least one AD user created (via LAM or samba-tool)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
User → Kasm login → LDAP bind (port 389) → Samba AD → credentials verified
                  → VM session (SSH/RDP/VNC) → credentials passed through

Kasm connects directly to Samba AD via LDAP. This is intentional — OIDC/SAML would provide SSO but cannot pass the actual password to VM sessions.

LDAP vs LDAPS

Samba AD supports both plaintext LDAP (port 389) and LDAPS (port 636). LDAPS uses a self-signed certificate generated during domain provisioning. Use ldaps://<nomad01-ip>:636 for encrypted connections. If the LDAP client requires a trusted CA, import the Samba auto-generated cert or use ldap:// on port 389 for simplicity on trusted networks.

docs.title: Step 1: Get Credentials from Vault
docs.text:
Retrieve the LDAP bind credentials:

# From your workstation (replace vault address as needed)
vault kv get -field=authentik_sync_password secret/samba-ad/service-accounts
vault kv get -field=authentik_sync_dn secret/samba-ad/service-accounts

Or via the API:

curl -sk -H "X-Vault-Token: <root-token>" \
  https://<nomad01-ip>:8200/v1/secret/data/samba-ad/service-accounts | \
  jq '.data.data | {authentik_sync_dn, authentik_sync_password}'

docs.title: Step 2: Configure LDAP in Kasm
docs.text:
1. Log in to the Kasm admin panel: https://kasm.<dns-suffix>
  2. Navigate to Access Management > Authentication > LDAP
  3. Click Add Configuration

Enter the following:

Field Value Name Samba AD URL ldap://<nomad01-ip>:389 Search Base DC=<domain>,DC=<tld> (e.g., DC=mylab,DC=lan) Search Filter (sAMAccountName=%(user)s) Group Search Filter (objectClass=group) Group Member Attribute member Search Subtree enabled Auto Create App User enabled Service Account DN CN=authentik-sync,CN=Users,DC=<domain>,DC=<tld> Service Account Password Value from Step 1
  1. Click Submit

docs.title: Step 3: Test Login
docs.text:
1. Log out of the Kasm admin panel
  2. On the login page, enter an AD username and password
  3. Verify login succeeds and the user dashboard loads
  4. Launch a VM session (SSH or RDP) and verify credentials pass through

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Group Mapping (Optional)
docs.text:
To map AD groups to Kasm groups:

  1. Navigate to Access Management > Groups
  2. Select a Kasm group (e.g., "All Users")
  3. Under LDAP Groups, add the AD group name (e.g., Domain Users)

docs.title: Connection fails
docs.text:
Test LDAP connectivity from a Nomad node:

# Install ldap-utils if needed
sudo apt-get install -y ldap-utils

# Test bind with service account
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<nomad01-ip>:389 \
  -D "CN=authentik-sync,CN=Users,DC=<domain>,DC=<tld>" \
  -w '<password>' \
  -b "DC=<domain>,DC=<tld>" \
  "(sAMAccountName=*)" sAMAccountName | head -20

docs.title: Login fails for specific users
docs.text:
Check if the user exists in AD:

# Find the Samba container
CID=$(docker ps --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | grep samba-ad | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')

# Look up user
docker exec $CID samba-tool user show <username>

docs.title: Credentials not passing through to VMs
docs.text:
This only works with LDAP authentication — not OIDC or SAML. Verify that:

  1. Kasm is configured for LDAP (not SAML/OIDC)
  2. The user logged in via the LDAP method (not local Kasm account)
  3. The VM session type supports credential passthrough (SSH, RDP, VNC)

docs.title: NAS Domain Join
docs.text: This tutorial explains how to join TrueNAS SCALE and Synology DSM to the Samba AD domain using the automated Terraform integration.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Domain joining is handled automatically by terraform/services/nas-domain-join.tf. When Samba AD is deployed and NAS servers are configured in bootstrap.yml, Terraform:

  1. Stores NAS credentials in Vault
  2. SSHes into nomad01 and runs the join logic via REST API
  3. Configures NAS DNS to point to Pi-hole (required for AD SRV record resolution)
  4. Joins the NAS to the AD domain using the domain-join-svc service account
  5. Polls for join completion

The join is idempotent: if the NAS is already joined to the correct domain, it is skipped.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Samba AD deployed (option 4)
  • NAS accessible from nomad01 on the network
  • For TrueNAS: API key generated in the TrueNAS UI
  • For Synology: DSM admin credentials

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add NAS servers to bootstrap.yml:

nas_servers:
  - name: "truenas-01"
    type: "truenas"
    address: "192.168.1.50"         # Management IP or FQDN
    api_key: "abc123..."             # TrueNAS API key

  - name: "synology-01"
    type: "synology"
    address: "192.168.1.51"
    admin_user: "admin"             # DSM admin username
    admin_password: "dsm-password"  # DSM admin password

docs.title: TrueNAS SCALE: Generating an API Key
docs.text:
1. Log in to TrueNAS SCALE web UI
  2. Navigate to System > API Keys
  3. Click Add
  4. Set a descriptive name (e.g., "proxmox-lab")
  5. Copy the generated key into bootstrap.yml

The API key is stored in Vault at secret/nas/truenas-01 after the first apply.

docs.title: Synology DSM: Preparation
docs.text:
The Synology DSM admin credentials are used for the initial API authentication only. The actual domain join uses the domain-join-svc service account created by Terraform.

Ensure: - DSM web UI is accessible on port 5001 (HTTPS) - The admin account has sufficient permissions (DSM Administrator)

docs.title: Applying the Configuration
docs.text:
After updating bootstrap.yml:

  1. Re-run option 1 to regenerate tfvars and apply, or:
  2. Re-apply Layer 2 Terraform if bootstrap has already run:
./setup.sh --dev
# d5) Deploy services

Or targeted: 

docker compose run terraform-services apply -auto-approve \
  -target=null_resource.nas_domain_join

docs.title: TrueNAS
docs.text:
1. Log in to TrueNAS UI
  2. Navigate to Credentials > Directory Services
  3. Verify: Active Directory is shown as Enabled with the correct domain

Or via API: 

curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer <api-key>" \
  "https://<truenas-ip>/api/v2.0/directoryservices" | jq .

docs.title: Synology
docs.text:
1. Log in to DSM
  2. Navigate to Control Panel > Domain/LDAP
  3. Verify: Domain is shown as joined

docs.title: Setting DNS on the NAS
docs.text:
The Terraform join logic sets the NAS DNS to the Pi-hole IP automatically. Verify this after joining:

TrueNAS: 

curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer <api-key>" \
  "https://<truenas-ip>/api/v2.0/network/configuration" | jq '.nameserver1'

Synology: Control Panel > Network > General > DNS Server

docs.title: Configuring User Home Directories
docs.text:
After domain join, configure where user home directories are created on the NAS:

TrueNAS SCALE: 1. Storage > Create Dataset: tank/homes 2. Sharing > Windows Shares > Add share pointing to the dataset 3. Credentials > Directory Services > AD: set Home Directory to the share

Synology DSM: 1. Control Panel > User and Group > Advanced 2. Enable user home service, set home path to a shared folder

docs.title: Configuring Profile Share (Roaming Profiles)
docs.text:
For roaming Windows profiles, configure in bootstrap.yml:

profile_server: "truenas.mylab.lan"
profile_share: "profiles"
profile_drive_letter: "P"

This creates a group policy object (via samba-ad-profiles.tf) that maps the profile share on domain login.

docs.title: TrueNAS: Cannot reach API
docs.text:
curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer <api-key>" \
  "https://<truenas-ip>/api/v2.0/system/info"

If this fails: verify the TrueNAS IP, that HTTPS is enabled, and the API key is correct.

docs.title: Domain join fails: DNS resolution
docs.text:
The NAS must be able to resolve Kerberos SRV records for the AD domain. These are served by Pi-hole, which forwards <ad-realm> queries to the Samba DC.

Test from nomad01: 

dig @<dns-01-ip> _ldap._tcp.<ad-realm-lowercase> SRV

If this fails, check that Pi-hole has the AD DNS forwarding rule: 

ssh labadmin@dns-01 "cat /etc/pihole/pihole.toml | grep -A5 ad_realm"

docs.title: Synology: Login failed
docs.text: Verify the admin username and password match the DSM account. The join uses port 5001 (HTTPS). If DSM uses a different port, update admin_password accordingly.

docs.title: Re-joining after Samba AD reset
docs.text:
If Samba AD data was wiped and redeployed (new domain), the NAS join state must also be reset:

TrueNAS: 1. UI: Credentials > Directory Services > Leave Domain, then re-join 2. Or remove Terraform state and re-apply: 

docker compose run terraform-services state rm null_resource.nas_domain_join[\"truenas-01\"]
docker compose run terraform-services apply -auto-approve

Synology: 1. Control Panel > Domain/LDAP > Leave Domain 2. Remove Terraform state and re-apply as above
